mainTopic: פיגול intent during only part of the מתיר, and whether a כהן's first intention carries over to later acts (רב against שמואל)
overview: This amud deals with offerings that become permitted through two things together, like the קומץ and the לבונה of a מנחה. In the משנה, רבי מאיר holds that פיגול intent during just one of them brings כרת. חכמים say there is no כרת unless the intent covers the entire מתיר. They agree when there is only one מתיר, and the same argument applies to the two כבשים of שבועות and the two בזיכין of לחם הפנים. In the גמרא, רב says the argument is only when the intent came last. If the intent was during the קומץ, everyone agrees it is פיגול, because a person acts on his first intention. שמואל says they argue either way. The גמרא challenges רב twice from ברייתות. The first one, about the קומץ, is answered by רב חנינא: two different כהנים did the two parts. The second ברייתא, about blood placed inside on יום הכיפורים, is answered by רבא and then by רב אשי. Each explains that the כהן repeated his intention, which shows it was not carrying over on its own.

steps.title: Improper intent during only the handful or only the frankincense
steps.stepSummary: רבי מאיר says פיגול intent during only the קומץ or only the לבונה makes the מנחה פיגול with כרת. חכמים require the intent to cover the whole מתיר.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the כהן had a פיגול intention while burning the handful but not the frankincense, or the frankincense but not the handful, רבי מאיר says it is פיגול and one who eats it gets כרת. The חכמים say there is no כרת unless he had the intention during the entire permitting process.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה opens with a מחלוקת about a מנחה that has two מתירים, the קומץ and the לבונה, where the improper intent happened during only one of them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A regular מנחה becomes permitted to eat only after both the קומץ and the לבונה are burned. רבי מאיר holds that half of the מתיר is enough to create פיגול. חכמים say that since the קומץ alone did not permit the מנחה, intent during it alone cannot bring כרת.

keyTerms.meaning: An offering ruined by the intention to eat it or burn it after its proper time. One who eats it gets כרת.
The handful of flour taken from a מנחה and burned on the מזבח
Frankincense that is burned along with the קומץ
Spiritual cutting off, a heavenly punishment
The permitting factor: the service that makes the offering allowed to eat

phrases.english: MISHNA
If he intended פיגול during the handful but not during the frankincense
phrases.notes: Here 'intended פיגול' means he burned it while planning to eat the rest of the מנחה after its time.

phrases.english: or during the frankincense but not during the handful
Rabbi Meir says: it is פיגול
and one is liable to כרת for eating it
And the Sages say: there is no כרת for it
unless he has the פיגול intent during the entire permitting factor

steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי מאיר: פיגול during half of the מתיר brings כרת. חכמים: there is no כרת unless the intent covers the whole מתיר.
steps.whatToRemember: The basic מחלוקת: can פיגול intent during part of the מתיר create כרת? רבי מאיר says yes, and חכמים say no.

steps.title: The Sages agree when the handful is the only permitting factor
steps.stepSummary: For מנחת חוטא and מנחת קנאות, which have no לבונה, חכמים agree that פיגול during the קומץ brings כרת.
steps.simpleTranslation: The חכמים agree with רבי מאיר about the sinner's מנחה and the סוטה's מנחה: if he had a פיגול intention during the handful, it is פיגול with כרת, because there the handful is the whole מתיר.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה shows where חכמים agree: in a מנחה with only one מתיר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: מנחת חוטא and מנחת קנאות have no לבונה, so the קומץ alone permits them. Intent during the קומץ therefore covers the entire מתיר. This shows the argument in step 1 is only about offerings with two מתירים.

keyTerms.meaning: The meal offering of a poor sinner, brought without oil or frankincense
The meal offering of a סוטה, also brought without frankincense
And they agree

phrases.english: And the Sages agree with Rabbi Meir
regarding the sinner's meal offering and the meal offering of jealousy
that if he intended פיגול during the handful
it is פיגול and one is liable to כרת for it
because the handful is the permitting factor

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the מחלוקת of step 1 to offerings that have two מתירים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When the קומץ is the only מתיר, פיגול during it brings כרת according to everyone.

steps.title: The same argument for the two lambs and the two frankincense bowls
steps.stepSummary: The same מחלוקת applies to slaughtering one of the two כבשים of שבועות with intent for the שתי הלחם, and to burning one of the two בזיכין with intent for the לחם הפנים.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he slaughtered one of the lambs intending to eat the two loaves the next day, or burned one of the bowls of frankincense intending to eat the two rows of bread the next day, רבי מאיר says it is פיגול with כרת. The חכמים say there is no כרת unless he had the intention during the entire מתיר.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה applies the same מחלוקת to two more offerings that each have a pair of מתירים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two כבשים together permit the שתי הלחם, and the two בזיכין together permit the לחם הפנים. Slaughtering only one lamb or burning only one bowl is half the מתיר, so רבי מאיר and חכמים argue just as in step 1.

keyTerms.meaning: The two lambs offered with the שתי הלחם on שבועות
The two loaves of שבועות (the שתי הלחם)
The two bowls of frankincense placed with the לחם הפנים
The two rows of the לחם הפנים

phrases.english: If he slaughtered one of the lambs
intending to eat the two loaves the next day
or if he burned one of the bowls of frankincense
intending to eat the two rows the next day
phrases.notes: The two rows here are the two stacks of לחם הפנים on the שולחן.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי מֵאִיר אוֹמֵר: פִּיגּוּל וְחַיָּיבִין עָלָיו כָּרֵת
phrases.english: Rabbi Meir says: it is פיגול and one is liable to כרת for it
And the Sages say: there is no כרת for it
unless he has the פיגול intent during the entire permitting factor

steps.triggerLanguage: שָׁחַט אֶחָד מִן הַכְּבָשִׂים לֶאֱכוֹל שְׁתֵּי חַלּוֹת לְמָחָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Extends the מחלוקת of step 1 to other offerings that have two מתירים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Intent during one of two lambs or one of two bowls is part of the מתיר. The same מחלוקת between רבי מאיר and חכמים applies.

steps.title: Intent about the slaughtered lamb itself versus intent about the other lamb
steps.stepSummary: Slaughtering one lamb with intent to eat it the next day makes that lamb פיגול, and the other lamb stays כשר. Intent to eat the other lamb leaves both כשר.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he slaughtered one of the lambs intending to eat from it the next day, that lamb is פיגול and the other is fine. If he intended to eat from the other lamb the next day, both are fine.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה finishes with a case where the intent concerns the meat of a lamb, not the loaves.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A lamb's own slaughter permits its own meat, so intent about its own meat makes it פיגול. One lamb does not permit the other lamb's meat. Each lamb is itself a מתיר, and one מתיר does not make another מתיר פיגול, so both stay כשר.

keyTerms.meaning: Its fellow, meaning the other lamb
Valid, a fit offering

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix this up with step 3. There the intent was about the loaves, which both lambs together permit. Here the intent is about the other lamb's meat, which this lamb does not permit at all.

phrases.english: If he slaughtered one of the lambs
intending to eat from it the next day
it is פיגול, and the other one is fit
If he intended to eat from the other one the next day
both are fit

steps.triggerLanguage: שָׁחַט אֶחָד מִן הַכְּבָשִׂים לֶאֱכוֹל מִמֶּנּוּ לְמָחָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Contrasts with step 3: intent about the lambs' meat instead of the loaves.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Intent about the slaughtered lamb's own meat makes only that lamb פיגול. Intent about the other lamb's meat leaves both lambs כשר.
steps.whatToRemember: פיגול works only through the service that actually permits the item in question. One lamb is not the מתיר for the other lamb.

steps.title: רב limits the dispute to silence first, then intent
steps.stepSummary: רב says the מחלוקת applies only when the קומץ was burned silently and the לבונה with פיגול intent. If the intent came first, during the קומץ, everyone agrees it is פיגול, because the first intention carries over.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב says: The argument is only where he burned the קומץ without saying anything, and then burned the לבונה with intent to eat the מנחה tomorrow. But if he burned the קומץ with that intent and then the לבונה silently, everyone agrees it is פיגול. Whatever a person does, he does with his first intention in mind.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens with רב explaining exactly which case רבי מאיר and חכמים argue about in the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the intent comes only at the end, during the לבונה, it clearly did not cover the קומץ, so חכמים say there is no כרת. If the intent was said during the קומץ, רב treats the silent לבונה as if the same intent was still in place. That means the whole מתיר was covered, and even חכמים agree it is פיגול.

keyTerms.meaning: In silence, with no stated intent
With intent (here, intent of פיגול)
Everyone agrees
Based on his first intention

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think רב is saying that silence counts as intent in every case. Silence only carries the intent forward when the intent was already stated earlier, during the קומץ. Silence that comes before any intent carries nothing.

phrases.english: GEMARA
Rav says: The dispute is
phrases.notes: The argument between רבי מאיר and חכמים in the משנה.

phrases.english: where he placed the handful in silence
and the frankincense with intent.
But if he placed the handful with intent
and the frankincense in silence,
all agree it is piggul,
for anyone who performs an act
performs it with his initial intent.
phrases.notes: So the silent לבונה is treated as if he still had the פיגול intent he said over the קומץ.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב: מַחְלוֹקֶת שֶׁנָּתַן אֶת הַקּוֹמֶץ בִּשְׁתִיקָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the גמרא by narrowing the case of the משנה's dispute (Step 1).
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The מחלוקת applies only when the intent was on the לבונה after a silent קומץ. Intent on the קומץ followed by a silent לבונה is פיגול according to everyone, because of על דעת ראשונה.

steps.title: שמואל says the dispute applies in both orders
steps.stepSummary: שמואל disagrees with רב. Even when the קומץ was burned with intent and the לבונה silently, רבי מאיר and חכמים still argue.
steps.simpleTranslation: And שמואל says: It is still a dispute.
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל argues with רב and says the second case is also part of the מחלוקת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל does not accept that the first intention automatically carries over to the silent לבונה. So in his view the intent covered only the קומץ, and חכמים would say there is no כרת.

keyTerms.meaning: Still
A dispute

phrases.english: And Shmuel says:
It is still a dispute.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with רב's limit on the case in Step 5.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Intent on the קומץ followed by a silent לבונה is still subject to the מחלוקת between רבי מאיר and חכמים.

steps.title: A ברייתא records the dispute even when the intent was on the קומץ
steps.stepSummary: רבא taught רב's view, and רב אחא בר רב הונא challenged him from a ברייתא. During the burning, the ברייתא lists both orders, including intent on the קומץ followed by a silent לבונה, and still records the מחלוקת. This fits שמואל, not רב.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא sat and taught this teaching. רב אחא בר רב הונא challenged רבא from a ברייתא: When does the rule apply that intent on the קומץ alone makes it פיגול? During the scooping of the handful, placing it in a vessel, and carrying it to the altar. When he comes to the burning, if he burned the קומץ silently and the לבונה with intent, or the קומץ with intent and the לבונה silently, רבי מאיר says it is פיגול and there is כרת. The חכמים say there is no כרת until he intends פיגול during the whole מתיר.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא teaches רב's rule, and a student attacks it with a ברייתא that seems to contradict it directly.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא first explains when the קומץ alone counts: during the early steps, which involve only the קומץ. Then, for the burning, it lists the case רב said everyone agrees on (intent on the קומץ, silent לבונה) and still says חכמים disagree. That matches שמואל and is a strong challenge to רב.

keyTerms.meaning: A teaching or ruling (here, רב's ruling)
In what case was this said? (limits a rule)
Scooping out the handful from the מנחה
Placing the קומץ into a service vessel
Carrying the vessel to the altar
Burning on the altar

steps.whyThisMatters: This objection puts רב's whole idea of על דעת ראשונה on the line. It sets up the next part of the גמרא, which will have to answer for רב.

phrases.english: Rava sat and was stating
this teaching,
phrases.notes: This is רב's teaching from Step 5.

phrases.aramaic: אֵיתִיבֵיהּ רַב אַחָא בַּר רַב הוּנָא לְרָבָא:
phrases.english: Rav Acha bar Rav Huna raised an objection to Rava:
In what case is this said?
During the removal of the handful, placing it in a vessel, and carrying it.
Once he comes to the burning,
if he placed the handful in silence
and the frankincense with intent,
or the handful with intent
and the frankincense in silence,
Rabbi Meir says:
It is piggul, and one is liable to karet for it,
and the Rabbis say: There is no karet
unless he has piggul intent during the entire permitting factor.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵיתִיבֵיהּ רַב אַחָא בַּר רַב הוּנָא לְרָבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רב's view (Step 5) as taught by רבא, using a ברייתא that fits שמואל (Step 6).
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's claim that intent on the קומץ followed by a silent לבונה is פיגול according to everyone.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא lists exactly that case during the burning and still records the חכמים saying there is no כרת. So it is not agreed by everyone.

steps.title: The challenge spelled out: intent first, silence second, and they still argue
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא בר רב הונא points to the exact case in the ברייתא: intent on the קומץ, silence on the לבונה, and רבי מאיר and חכמים still argue. This goes against רב.
steps.simpleTranslation: In any event, the ברייתא teaches a case where he placed the קומץ with intent and the לבונה in silence, and they still disagree.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing the challenge from Step 7 by quoting the exact case in the ברייתא that causes the problem for רב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב said that when the intention comes first, during the קומץ, it carries over to the לבונה, so everyone agrees it is פיגול. The ברייתא has exactly that order and still records a מחלוקת. So the first intention does not seem to carry over, which fits שמואל.

keyTerms.meaning: Intention, here a פיגול intention to eat the offering after its proper time
And they disagree

phrases.english: In any event, it teaches:
He placed the handful with intent
and the frankincense in silence,
and they disagree.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the קשיא begun in Step 7 by pointing to the exact clause in the ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's claim (Step 5) that intent during the קומץ carries over to a silent לבונה, so everyone agrees it is פיגול.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא has the very case רב described, intent first and silence second, and still says there is a מחלוקת.

steps.title: רבא: the לבונה had already been burned earlier
steps.stepSummary: רבא rereads the ברייתא: the silent לבונה was burned before the קומץ, so there was no earlier intention to carry over.
steps.simpleTranslation: Say that the case is where he had already burned the לבונה in silence from the start, before the קומץ.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא defends רב by saying the ברייתא's case has a different order than it seems: the לבונה was burned first.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the silent לבונה came first, then no intention existed yet that could carry over to it. So the case does not contradict רב, who only spoke about intent that came first. The מחלוקת in the ברייתא is then about a case רב agrees is disputed.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Say', a reading of the source in a different way to remove a difficulty
From the start, earlier

phrases.english: Say: and he had already placed the frankincense
in silence from the start.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵימָא: וּכְבָר נָתַן אֶת הַלְּבוֹנָה בִּשְׁתִיקָה מֵעִיקָּרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 8 on behalf of רב.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpreting the order of events in the ברייתא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא describes intent on the קומץ followed by a silent לבונה.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא describes a silent לבונה burned earlier, so רב's carry-over rule does not apply.

steps.title: Two reasons רבא's answer fails
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects רבא's reading. First, it would make this case the same as the ברייתא's first case. Second, another ברייתא clearly says the לבונה was burned afterward.
steps.simpleTranslation: There are two answers against this. One: this would be the same as the first case. And also, a ברייתא clearly says 'afterward.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא knocks down רבא's answer with two separate arguments.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא already taught a case where the silent part came first, so רבא's reading makes the second case say nothing new. On top of that, another ברייתא uses the word 'afterward', which shows the silent לבונה really came after the קומץ with intent. So the challenge against רב comes back.

keyTerms.meaning: There are two refutations of this idea
The first one, here meaning the first case of the ברייתא
Afterward

steps.confusionAlert: The two refutations are separate. The first is about repeating a case, and the second is about the wording of a different ברייתא.

phrases.english: There are two refutations of this:
One, that this is the same as the first case,
And also, isn't it taught: 'afterward'?
phrases.notes: Another ברייתא says he burned the לבונה after the קומץ, so it clearly came second.

steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: It makes the ברייתא repeat itself, and it goes against another ברייתא that says 'afterward.'

steps.title: רב חנינא: two different people, two separate minds
steps.stepSummary: רב חנינא explains the ברייתא in a way that fits רב: one כהן burned the קומץ with intent and a different כהן burned the לבונה in silence.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חנינא explained the ברייתא as a case of two separate minds.
steps.whatsHappening: After רבא's answer failed, רב חנינא gives a new answer to defend רב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב's carry-over rule only works when the same person does both parts, because then his first intention continues. If two different כהנים did the two parts, the second one's silence has nothing to do with the first one's intention. So the ברייתא's מחלוקת does not contradict רב.

keyTerms.meaning: He explained it, he interpreted the source
Two minds, meaning two different people with separate intentions

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the limit of רב's rule: an intention carries over only within one person's actions.

phrases.english: Rav Chanina explained it
as a case of two minds.
phrases.notes: Two different כהנים, one burning the קומץ and the other burning the לבונה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a new defense of רב after רבא's defense was rejected in Step 10.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the ברייתא to a special case (two כהנים)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא is about one כהן doing both parts, which goes against רב.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא is about two כהנים, where the intention cannot carry over, so it fits רב.

steps.title: A new proof begins: blood placed on the outer מזבח
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא starts a new proof for שמואל from a ברייתא about פיגול during the placing of blood on the outer מזבח.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: In what case is this said? With blood that is placed on the outer מזבח.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up a new proof for שמואל, quoting the start of a ברייתא about blood. The full argument comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא is about blood that is placed on the outer מזבח, where one placement is enough to make the offering permitted. The גמרא is moving from the קומץ and לבונה to the case of blood to test the same question. Steps 13-14 show how this supports שמואל.

keyTerms.meaning: Blood of the offerings
The outer altar in the courtyard

phrases.english: Come and hear:
In what case are these words said?
With blood that is placed on the outer altar.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the ברייתא about the קומץ was explained in a way that fits רב, the גמרא turns to a new source to support שמואל.
steps.raayaObject: שמואל's view that intent does not carry over, and the מחלוקת applies in both orders.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא about פיגול intent during the placements of blood on the outer מזבח.

steps.title: The ברייתא continues: inner-altar blood placements
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא moves to blood placed inside, like on יום הכיפורים. If the פיגול intention was in any one of the sets, רבי מאיר says it is פיגול with כרת, and חכמים say there is no כרת unless the intention covered the whole מתיר.
steps.simpleTranslation: But blood placed on the inner מזבח, like the forty-three placements of יום הכיפורים, the eleven of the anointed כהן's bull, and the eleven of the community's bull: if he had a פיגול intention in the first, second or third set, רבי מאיר says it is פיגול and one gets כרת. חכמים say there is no כרת until he has the intention during the whole מתיר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא keeps quoting the ברייתא it started in step 12, now moving from the outer מזבח to the inner one. This is the part of the ברייתא that the proof for שמואל will rest on.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Inside offerings need several sets of blood placements, and together they make up the מתיר (the act that makes the offering permitted). The ברייתא says the argument happens even when the intention was in only one set. חכמים require the intention during every part of the מתיר before there is כרת.

keyTerms.meaning: The inner (golden) altar inside the היכל
The bull brought by the כהן גדול for a sin done by mistake
The bull brought when the community sinned because of a mistaken ruling

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל דָּמִים הַנִּיתָּנִין עַל מִזְבֵּחַ הַפְּנִימִי,
phrases.english: But blood that is placed on the inner altar,

phrases.aramaic: כְּגוֹן אַרְבָּעִים וְשָׁלֹשׁ שֶׁל יוֹם הַכִּיפּוּרִים,
phrases.english: for example, the forty-three of Yom Kippur,
phrases.notes: These are the forty-three placements of blood from the bull and the goat of יום הכיפורים.

phrases.aramaic: וְאַחַת עֶשְׂרֵה שֶׁל פַּר כֹּהֵן מָשׁוּחַ,
phrases.english: and the eleven of the bull of the anointed priest,

phrases.aramaic: וְאַחַת עֶשְׂרֵה שֶׁל פַּר הֶעְלֵם דָּבָר שֶׁל צִיבּוּר,
phrases.english: and the eleven of the bull for a communal mistaken ruling,
if he had a piggul intention, whether in the first
whether in the second or whether in the third,
phrases.notes: First, second and third mean the different sets of blood placements, for example inside the קודש הקדשים, on the curtain, and on the inner מזבח.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי מֵאִיר אוֹמֵר: פִּיגּוּל וְחַיָּיבִין עָלָיו כָּרֵת,
phrases.english: Rabbi Meir says: It is piggul, and one is liable to karet for it,
and the Rabbis say: There is no karet for it
until he has the piggul intention during the entire permitting service.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲבָל דָּמִים הַנִּיתָּנִין עַל מִזְבֵּחַ הַפְּנִימִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes quoting the ברייתא that step 12 started.
steps.raayaObject: שמואל's view that a כהן is not assumed to keep his first intention, so חכמים argue even when the intention was in only one set
steps.raayaSupportSource: ברייתא about the inner-altar blood placements

steps.title: The point of the proof: they argue even with intent in just one set
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא points to the wording: the intention was in only one of the sets, and רבי מאיר and חכמים still argue. That goes against רב.
steps.simpleTranslation: In any case, it teaches: he had a פיגול intention in the first, second or third set, and they argue.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא spells out exactly where the proof is in the ברייתא it just quoted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רב, חכמים hold that a כהן keeps acting on his first intention, so an intention in the first set should count for every set. Yet the ברייתא says חכמים give no כרת when the intention was in only one set. That suggests חכמים do not hold 'he acts on his first intention', which is שמואל's view.

keyTerms.meaning: In any case, at least (used to focus on the key point)
They argue

phrases.english: In any case, it teaches:
if he had a piggul intention, whether in the first, whether in the second,
or whether in the third, and they argue.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the proof out of the ברייתא quoted in steps 12-13.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא's words 'whether in the first, second or third' together with the argument between רבי מאיר and חכמים

steps.title: The two-priests answer may not work here
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא expects someone to answer, like רב חנינא did, that two different כהנים did the placements. That only works for the view that a new כהן גדול may continue with the first bull's blood. For the view that he may not, the answer fails.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you say that here too there are two minds (two כהנים), that works for the one who says 'with a bull' means even with the bull's blood. But for the one who says 'with a bull' and not with its blood, what can you say?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא blocks a likely way out of the proof, so the challenge against רב stays strong.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 11, רב חנינא saved רב by saying a second כהן finished the service, so there was no first intention to carry over. Here that only works if a replacement כהן גדול may continue with blood the first one already collected. Some learn from the פסוק 'בְּפַר' that he must start over with a new bull, so on that view two כהנים could never share these placements.

keyTerms.meaning: Two minds, meaning two different כהנים each with his own intention
With the blood of the bull, meaning blood another כהן already prepared
That works out fine (for one view)
What can be said? (there seems to be no answer)

phrases.aramaic: וְכִי תֵּימָא, הָכָא נָמֵי בִּשְׁתֵּי דֵּעוֹת –
phrases.english: And if you would say: here too it is with two minds,
phrases.notes: This is רב חנינא's answer from step 11, where one כהן started and a different כהן finished.

phrases.english: that works out for the one who says "with a bull"
means even with the blood of a bull,
phrases.notes: ויקרא 16:3. On this view, a replacement כהן גדול may go in with the blood of the bull the first one slaughtered.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא לְמַאן דְּאָמַר ״בְּפַר״ וְלֹא בְּדָמוֹ שֶׁל פַּר,
phrases.english: but according to the one who says "with a bull" and not with the blood of a bull,
what is there to say?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי תֵּימָא, הָכָא נָמֵי בִּשְׁתֵּי דֵּעוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shuts down the expected 'two כהנים' defense of רב against the proof in step 14.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Partial: the 'two minds' answer works on one view but not the other.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: For the view that a replacement כהן גדול may not use the first bull's blood, two different כהנים cannot share the placements, so the ברייתא cannot be read that way.

steps.title: רבא: he repeated the intention in the third set
steps.stepSummary: רבא explains the ברייתא in a way that fits רב. The כהן had the intention in the first set, was silent in the second, and had it again in the third. Repeating it shows he did not do the second set with his first intention.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: What case are we dealing with? He had a פיגול intention in the first set, was silent in the second, and had it again in the third. We say: if you think anyone who acts does so with his first intention, why would he need to repeat the intention in the third set?
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives a new answer for רב, explaining which exact case the ברייתא means.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב's rule, that a person acts on his first intention, is only a default assumption. Here the כהן himself showed otherwise: by stating the intention again in the third set, he showed the silent second set was not done with that intention. So the intention did not cover the whole מתיר, and חכמים rightly say there is no כרת, even according to רב.

keyTerms.meaning: What case are we dealing with here? (used to narrow the case)
He was silent, meaning he had no stated intention

keyTerms.term: כָּל הָעוֹשֶׂה עַל דַּעַת רִאשׁוֹנָה הוּא עוֹשֶׂה
keyTerms.meaning: Anyone who acts does so with his first intention (רב's principle)
If it enters your mind (if you were to think)
To go back and repeat

steps.whatToRemember: רב's rule that a כהן keeps his first intention is only a default. If the כהן repeats the intention later, that shows the silent part in between was not done with it.
steps.confusionAlert: רבא is not saying the second set was done with a proper intention. He is saying that the repeated intention shows the כהן's first intention was not running during the silent second set, so the פיגול intention did not cover the whole מתיר.

phrases.english: Rava said: Here, what are we dealing with?
For example, where he had a piggul intention in the first set,
and was silent in the second, and had a piggul intention in the third,
where we say: If it enters your mind that

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל הָעוֹשֶׂה עַל דַּעַת רִאשׁוֹנָה הוּא עוֹשֶׂה,
phrases.english: anyone who acts does so with his first intention,
why do I need him to repeat the piggul intention in the third?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the proof against רב (steps 13-14) after the 'two כהנים' answer was blocked in step 15.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא proves that חכמים do not hold 'he acts on his first intention', which would go against רב.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא is about a כהן who repeated his intention in the third set. That shows he was not acting on his first intention during the silent second set, so חכמים agree there is no כרת even according to רב.

steps.title: רב אשי: The ברייתא Never Mentions Silence
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי challenges רבא's explanation, because the ברייתא does not say the כהן was silent.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי objects: Does the ברייתא say anything about him being silent?
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי attacks רבא's answer from step 16. רבא's whole case depends on the כהן being silent in the second set, but the ברייתא never says that.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא needed a silent middle set to make his reading work. רב אשי points out that this detail is not in the words of the ברייתא at all. So רבא is reading in a key fact that the text never gives.

keyTerms.meaning: Objects to it; raises a strong challenge against a statement
Was silent; did the act without saying any intention
Does it teach anything about...? A way of saying the text does not say this

phrases.english: Rav Ashi objects to this:
Does it teach anything about being silent?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רַב אָשֵׁי: מִידֵּי שָׁתַק קָתָנֵי
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's reading that the כהן was silent in the second set.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא's wording never mentions silence, so רבא's case is not what the text describes.

steps.title: רב אשי: He Repeated the Intention in the First Three
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי explains the ברייתא differently. The כהן said his פיגול intention in the first, second, and third placings. Repeating it shows he does not count on his first intention carrying over.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רב אשי said: Here we are dealing with a case where he had פיגול intention in the first, second, and third placings. Then we say: If you think a person always acts based on his first intention, why did he need to repeat the פיגול intention in the second and third?
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי gives his own case so that the ברייתא still fits רב. The כהן spoke his intention in the first three placings and stayed quiet for the rest.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the first intention carried over by itself, there would be no reason to say it again in the second and third placings. Since he did repeat it, this shows that the later placings, where he was silent, were not done with that intention. This is the reasoning for the side that says there is no כרת, and it does not need to read silence into the ברייתא the way רבא's case did.

keyTerms.meaning: He had פיגול intention, meaning a wrong thought about eating the offering at the wrong time
Why do I need it? Pointing out that something would be unnecessary

steps.whatToRemember: רב אשי's case: the כהן said his פיגול intention in the first three placings. Repeating it proves he does not rely on his first intention, so the later silent placings do not count as done with that intention.

phrases.english: Rather, Rav Ashi said:
Here, what are we dealing with?
Such as where he had פיגול intention in the first
phrases.notes: He means the first placing of the blood, and he stayed silent for the placings after the third.

phrases.english: and in the second and in the third,
where we say:
If it enters your mind

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל הָעוֹשֶׂה עַל דַּעַת רִאשׁוֹנָה הוּא עוֹשֶׂה,
phrases.english: that anyone who does an act does it based on his first intention,
then to go back and have פיגול intention in the second and third
why do I need it?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָמַר רַב אָשֵׁי: הָכָא בְּמַאי עָסְקִינַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces רבא's rejected case with a new case that fits the wording of the ברייתא.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Re-defining the case of the ברייתא (הָכָא בְּמַאי עָסְקִינַן)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא seemed to describe intention in only one set, with רבי מאיר and חכמים still arguing, which goes against רב. רבא's silent-middle case was not in the text.
steps.terutzMaskana: The כהן spoke his intention in the first three placings. His repeating shows the later silent placings were not done with that intention, so the ברייתא fits רב without adding silence that the text does not mention.
